title: The speed of light in vacuum is an exact constant

body: The 2022 CODATA recommended values, published by NIST, list the speed of light in vacuum as 299,792,458 metres per second. The standard uncertainty is given as exact, and the relative standard uncertainty is exact. An exact uncertainty means the number is a defined constant in the system of units, not a measurement that still has an error bar. This card reports that CODATA entry. It does not retell the 1983 redefinition of the metre, which is a related standards decision not quoted here. Because the value is exact by definition, more precise experiments do not revise these digits; they would revise how the units are realized in the laboratory.
